result.headline: Motor outputs dropped to minimum at t=76.1 s, before the logged kill-switch event, during an AUTO_LAND descent.
result.explanation: Offboard control ended (AUTO_LAND at 69.8 s). All motor outputs stepped to 900/0 us at 76.122 s, 0.79 s before 'Manual kill-switch engaged'. The recording does not show who or what commanded the kill.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch1] at t=76.122 s: 1608.5 -> 900 us (step -708.5, 50.6x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Motor output fell to minimum with no ramp. ch2-ch4 did the same, and ch5/ch6 went 1500 -> 0 (lines 47, 49, 51, 53, 54).

evidence.quote: EVENT t=76.915 s controller.event[log] ERROR: [commander] Manual kill-switch engaged
evidence.shows: The logged kill event comes after the output drop (76.122 s). Both occur after the AUTO_LAND switch.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=69.847 s controller.event[vehicle_status] nav_state OFFBOARD -> AUTO_LAND
evidence.shows: A mode change is the earliest event. The first signals to leave baseline follow at 70.15 s (roll setpoint) and 70.234 s (ch1-3).

evidence.quote: EVENT t=70.362 s controller.event[log] ERROR: [mavlink] [timesync] Time jump detected. Resetting time synchroniser.
evidence.shows: Time-sync reset 0.5 s after the mode change. This points to the offboard/companion link or clock, but the data does not link it to the kill.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.attitude[yaw] followed its setpoint worse for good from t=72.579 s: typical |error| 0.106 before, 0.393 after deg (4.2x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Attitude tracking degraded from about 72.6 s, before the kill, with no actuator freeze. Yaw-rate error ratio is 2.27 and roll 1.73 across 73.584 s. This is consistent with a rough landing descent.

checked.check: Sequence of first departures from baseline, 70-78 s
checked.result: Roll setpoint (70.15 s), ch1-3 (70.234 s) and roll attitude (70.281 s) moved first. ch5/ch6 went to 0 at 76.934 s and ch4 at 76.627 s. The logged kill event is at 76.915 s.
checked.about: Cause versus effect around the kill

checked.result: Nothing is frozen. Altitude estimate fell 3.144 -> 0.162 m, the expected descent. Actuator spread rose. Tracking error roughly doubled for yaw rate and rose 1.7x for roll.
checked.about: Sensor or estimator freeze as the cause

checked.result: No lessons. The battery and HV family does not apply (px4_vehicle). Charge accounting is indeterminate and the other physical checks are not applicable.

checked.check: Start-up events and takeoff shifts at 2-8 s
checked.result: Altitude, attitude and tracking shifts sit at the takeoff transient. Nothing later points back to them.

outcomes.label: Operator kill command precedes 76.122 s
outcomes.means: The cut was commanded. The remaining question is why the pilot killed during AUTO_LAND.
outcomes.then: Review the operator and RC procedure with the pilot.

outcomes.label: No kill command; a failsafe or offboard command
outcomes.means: The cut came from the control or link side, not the operator.
outcomes.then: Trace the time-jump and offboard link.

outcomes.label: No command at all before the output drop
outcomes.means: The cut came without a recorded command, which points at the output or ESC path.
outcomes.then: Request ESC and actuator-driver logs and a bench check.

provenance.status: passed the action gate; not a validated procedure

safety_findings.statement: Recorded SOC went 86.19 % -> 60.61 % over 79.09 s while measured charge was only 0.0021 Ah (0.013 pp). The SOC estimate is not trustworthy here and is not used as evidence.

unknowns: Who or what commanded the output drop at 76.122 s: the recording does not show it.
Why the logged kill event is 0.79 s after the output drop (log timestamp offset or a different trigger).
Why the vehicle was switched from OFFBOARD to AUTO_LAND at 69.847 s.

already_answered.question: When did the outputs drop, and did a mode change come first?
already_answered.answer: Yes. OFFBOARD -> AUTO_LAND at 69.847 s. The outputs fell to minimum at 76.122 s, then the kill event, landing and disarm followed.
already_answered.quote: EVENT t=69.847 s controller.event[vehicle_status] nav_state OFFBOARD -> AUTO_LAND

already_answered.question: Did any output freeze before the incident?
already_answered.answer: No frozen outputs after 73.584 s. ch5/ch6 held 1500 until 76.833 s, and ch7/ch8 were 0 throughout.
already_answered.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch5] held 1500 from t=0.706 to 76.833 s (709 samples)

field_questions.question: Did the pilot deliberately press the kill switch, and at what moment relative to touchdown?
field_questions.why_needed: Separates an operator-commanded kill from a spurious or automatic cut.
field_questions.not_in_data: Searched events and the sheet for RC or command signals. Only the commander message appears, with no source, so the data cannot say who pressed it.

if_answers.means: An operator-commanded cut. The timing offset is likely a log-time artefact.
A spurious kill input, a failsafe or a link-side command is more likely.

data_requests.what: Full ulog topics for command source, failsafe flags and RC input
data_requests.why_needed: Identifies who commanded the output drop at 76.122 s.

unobservable.fact: Whether the kill switch or RC link was physically actuated or glitched
unobservable.why_it_matters: Separates an operator kill from a spurious input.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Interview the pilot, check the RC transmitter switch state and the link log.

unobservable.why_it_matters: An output-stage fault would look like a cut without a command.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-test the ESCs and read the ESC telemetry if available.

hypotheses.claim: A deliberate or accidental manual kill-switch input cut the motor outputs during AUTO_LAND.
hypotheses.because: The kill event at 76.915 s is logged and outputs cut at 76.122 s. The 0.79 s offset and the missing command source leave this unproven.
hypotheses.observed_at: commander log and actuator output readings

hypotheses.claim: The offboard or companion link lost sync, causing the AUTO_LAND switch, and a failsafe or command cut the outputs.
hypotheses.because: The time-jump error at 70.362 s follows the mode change at 69.847 s. Whether the time-jump caused the mode change or is an effect of it cannot be told from this data.

hypotheses.claim: An output-stage or ESC fault dropped the outputs without a command.
hypotheses.because: Outputs went from normal to 900/0 us at once, but this is also the pattern of a commanded kill. No signal observes the ESCs.

hypotheses.claim: An estimator or sensor fault triggered the landing and the cut.
hypotheses.because: No signal froze. The altitude estimate fell 3.144 -> 0.162 m as expected for a descent. Tracking degraded only moderately.

events.what: Takeoff-time level shifts and attitude/yaw-rate tracking error at 2-12 s
events.why: Takeoff transient. Nothing later points back to it.
Earliest mode change. The reason is not recorded.
Possible link or clock issue 0.5 s after the mode change.

events.what: All motor outputs stepped to 900/0 us at 76.122 s
events.why: Abrupt cut without a recorded commander.
Logged 0.79 s after the output cut; source unknown.

events.what: Yaw and yaw-rate tracking degraded from 72.6 s
events.why: Likely descent or landing dynamics and the cut.

result.lesson: No earlier cases apply; none are stored for this signature.
result.reuse_when: Another PX4 vehicle, in the same firmware and offboard configuration, shows outputs dropping to minimum during AUTO_LAND shortly after a timesync reset and before the kill-switch event.

constrained_claims.text: Motor outputs dropped to minimum at t=76.1 s, before the logged kill-switch event, during an AUTO_LAND descent.

Offboard control ended (AUTO_LAND at 69.8 s). All motor outputs stepped to 900/0 us at 76.122 s, 0.79 s before 'Manual kill-switch engaged'. The recording does not show who or what commanded the kill.
Operator / manual kill: A deliberate or accidental manual kill-switch input cut the motor outputs during AUTO_LAND.
